articles.title: 13,000-Year-Old Bones Show Ancient Hunters Butchered Elephant-Like Beasts
articles.summary: Archaeologists in Chile found 13,000-year-old bones with cut marks from stone tools. The bones belonged to gomphotheres — extinct elephant relatives — and show that some of the first people in South America hunted and ate them.

articles.title: Why Do You Feel Tired After a Wild Dream? Scientists May Have Found Out
articles.summary: Scientists watched mice sleep and found something weird: during REM sleep, when we dream, the brain's fuel supply goes up — but the energy neurons actually use goes down. That may explain why vivid dreams can leave you exhausted.

articles.title: CERN Starts Taking Apart the World's Biggest Atom Smasher
articles.summary: The Large Hadron Collider, a 27-kilometer ring under Europe, is getting a major upgrade. Crews have started removing 28 giant magnets to replace them with stronger ones that will create more particle collisions.
